basis: Immune-mediated inflammation of the small intestine; extraintestinal damage is not common enough to label across this group.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the respiratory system; metastatic organs are not inherent across the group.
CoQ10 deficiency with defining encephalomyopathy; cardiomyopathy defines the syndrome, reduced LVEF in 1/2. Hearing loss 10/14 omitted by cap; respiratory failure may be neuromuscular.
Malignant astrocytic tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Progressive tubulointerstitial kidney injury. Anemia is secondary to renal failure; frequent retinal pigmentation alone does not establish functional eye damage.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; central origin does not establish neurologic damage.
Congenital platelet and erythroid production disorder with thrombocytopenia, dyserythropoiesis and anemia.
Inherited central choroidal dystrophy affecting the eye.
Isolated sperm structural and motility defects causing male infertility; reproductive function has no axis.
Tumor of the oropharynx; the specified axes assign the pharynx to pulmonary.
Neutral amino-acid transport failure in kidney and intestine; neurologic dysfunction includes ataxia annotated 80-99%. Skin rash may be transient; ocular signs lack clear direct damage.
Regional loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue defines this metabolic disorder; diabetes and fatty liver are separate associated diseases.
Adenovirus infection directly involving the kidney or urinary tract.
Congenital fibular absence and split-hand/foot malformations define a skeletal disorder.
Defining renal phosphate wasting causes hypophosphatemia, with nephrolithiasis and osteoporosis forming the disease phenotype.
Defining hepatic/cardiac syndrome with palatal clefting 2/2; hearing loss 2/2 supports otologic. Renal and neurologic lesions each reported in single patients omitted by cap.
Neoplasm directly occupying the optic nerve, which is assigned to the ocular axis.
Dyskeratosis congenita is defined by marrow failure, nail dystrophy and oral leukoplakia; aplastic anemia in 2/3. Other organ findings lack reliable subtype frequencies.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic MERTK variants.
Congenital split spinal cord; associated scoliosis is frequent (30-79%). Local hirsutism does not establish damaging skin disease.
Bone fragility with osteoporosis and recurrent fractures in 2/2; syringomyelia in 1/2 supports neurologic involvement, though the reported cohort is very small.
Type 1 is a supraglottic interarytenoid cleft above the vocal folds; the definition does not establish an esophageal defect.
Autoimmune central, autonomic and peripheral nerve hyperexcitability syndrome, commonly associated with CASPR2 antibodies; muscle cramps reflect neural dysfunction.
Intellectual disability and characteristic skeletal anomalies define it; strabismus 7/11 and kidney abnormalities 30-79% support involvement. Dental anomalies >30% omitted by cap.
CLCN4-related neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, seizures and cerebral abnormalities; ocular and skeletal findings are occasional (5-29%).
